name: The Afghan Whigs
label: Sub Pop
lede: A Cincinnati bar band that wanted to be the Temptations, Neil Young and the Band at once, signed by a Seattle grunge label, broken by a fractured skull and a press release, and still going forty years on.

eras.title: A better bassist than the last one
eras.text: Greg Dulli came home to Cincinnati from film school and a Tower Records job in Los Angeles and started the Black Republicans. Out of that band came the Afghan Whigs: a punk band that wanted to play soul, and got a Seattle label to listen.

q: I'm better than your bass player.
John Curley, as Greg Dulli tells it
years.h: John Curley tells Greg Dulli he's better than Dulli's bassist
years.p: After a Black Republicans show in Cincinnati, [[John Curley|1d7ed8e7-199f-4774-b7a2-99a0feebf55a]] walked up to [[Greg Dulli|0b17f0c3-9e37-4863-ab92-2c5be31e6e53]] and said he could outplay the band's bass player. Dulli said fine.
years.xp: Dulli had dropped out of film school at the University of Cincinnati, moved to Los Angeles, worked at Tower Records on Sunset and tried acting. Seeing [[The Dream Syndicate|8577c385-d06a-4a64-b4e7-6ebf25f2cb20]] sent him back to Ohio to start a band.

years.h: The Afghan Whigs form, named as a joke on the Black Republicans
years.p: Greg Dulli, John Curley, effects-pedal guitarist [[Rick McCollum|24875099-22a5-45aa-aae1-bf341ffd7e59]] and drummer [[Steve Earle|ceed50f1-a8d7-443e-8204-392dcab13970]]. John Curley coined the name as a play on Dulli's old band.
years.xp:
The first song they rehearsed was the Temptations' Psychedelic Shack. Dulli described the target as a cross between the Band, the Temptations, and Neil Young with Crazy Horse.

Rick McCollum was already known around Cincinnati for what he could do with a floor full of pedals.

years.h: Big Top Halloween: 1,000 self-pressed copies on Ultrasuede
years.p: The Afghan Whigs put out their debut themselves. Greg Dulli had written half of it in Arizona after the Black Republicans broke up, and one copy reached Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman.

years.h: Sub Pop signs its second band from outside the Northwest
years.p: Only Denver's The Fluid got there first. Greg Dulli credits the Fluid for opening Sub Pop's door to the Afghan Whigs, from Cincinnati.

eras.title: Soul records on a grunge label
eras.text: On Sub Pop the Afghan Whigs sat next to Mudhoney and Nirvana but sounded like a Motown record played through a fuzz box. Congregation found the voice, MTV found the videos, and the majors came calling.

years.h: Up in It: Jack Endino at the desk
years.p: The Afghan Whigs' Sub Pop debut, produced by [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]], Nirvana's producer. Retarded becomes a college-radio hit.

years.h: On the road with Mudhoney and Bullet LaVolta
years.p: The Afghan Whigs tour Up in It on a Sub Pop package bill with [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]] and Boston's Bullet LaVolta.

years.h: Greg Dulli records "Miles Iz Ded" the day Miles Davis dies
years.p: At Ultrasuede in Cincinnati, Dulli cuts a hidden track for Congregation built around a message from label man David Katznelson.

years.h: Congregation: a $15,000 advance and the real sound
years.p: Made July to September 1991 at Bear Creek near Seattle, in Los Angeles and in Cincinnati on a $15,000 Sub Pop advance. Soul, psychedelic sprawl and punk in one band.
years.xp:
The cover photo shows a nude Black woman on a blanket holding a white baby, read by many as a comment on the band's debt to Black music. Greg Dulli co-produced with Ross Ian Stein.

It didn't chart, but the videos for Turn On the Water and Conjure Me got onto MTV, and the band toured North America and Europe, including dates with [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]].

years.h: Uptown Avondale: the Afghan Whigs cover the Supremes
years.p: A covers EP named for a Cincinnati neighborhood, with Supremes songs done the Afghan Whigs way. The Conjure Me single carries a Supremes cover too.

years.h: The Afghan Whigs leave Sub Pop for Elektra
years.p: On the back of Congregation's MTV play and cult following, the Afghan Whigs sign to Elektra Records.

eras.title: Gentlemen, and what came after
eras.text: On a major label, Greg Dulli made a breakup record that turned the camera on the man doing the damage. Gentlemen is the one people press on their friends; Black Love went darker, into noir and crime scenes.

years.h: Gentlemen: cut at Ardent in Memphis, Big Star's studio
years.p: Greg Dulli produced it himself at Ardent Studios and Ultrasuede. A song cycle about a relationship going bad, with an ironic title.
years.xp:
The cover is modeled on Nan Goldin's 1983 photo Nan and Brian in Bed. Wikipedia says Linda Ronstadt, also on Elektra, objected to it as close to pornographic.

Debonair went Top 20 on the Modern Rock chart. The album placed No. 17 in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop poll, and by 1996 had sold 130,000 US copies.

years.h: Greg Dulli can't sing "My Curse," so Marcy Mays does
years.p: The Gentlemen song about a violent breakup was so personal that Greg Dulli handed the lead vocal to [[Scrawl|c5e3744d-b321-4cc9-976a-4d4d9d0ee73a]]'s [[Marcy Mays|5aac1027-892f-4d12-8dc3-ebb54de02a3c]].
years.xp: Mays had already sung on the Afghan Whigs' Ornament single. On My Curse the man's side of the story comes out of a woman's mouth, which is the whole point of Gentlemen: the narrator is the problem.

years.h: Greg Dulli hangs up on Don Was, then sings John Lennon in Backbeat
years.p: Hungover in a hotel room, Dulli thought the call was a prank. He ended up singing most leads on the Beatles biopic soundtrack with [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]], [[Mike Mills|525d2a4a-3d81-4d96-9581-3442feed3d2e]] and Don Fleming.
years.xp: The band cut the whole soundtrack live in two days, playing the covers the Beatles did in Hamburg.

years.h: Greg Dulli, the only guest on Foo Fighters' debut
years.p: Dave Grohl asked Greg Dulli to play guitar during an afternoon session. Dulli is the only credited musician on Foo Fighters besides Grohl, and says he barely remembers it.

years.h: Steve Earle out, Paul Buchignani drums on Black Love
years.p: Original drummer Steve Earle leaves after Gentlemen. Paul Buchignani plays as the Afghan Whigs start Black Love in Seattle and Memphis.

years.h: Black Love: James Ellroy, Hollywood Babylon, Weegee
years.p: Greg Dulli's noir record, reaching No. 79 on the Billboard 200. Blame, Etc. draws on the life of Temptations singer David Ruffin.
years.xp: Dulli pulled from Ellroy's crime novels, the Coen brothers' Blood Simple, Kenneth Anger's Hollywood Babylon and Weegee's crime-scene photos. Crime Scene Part One was reportedly influenced by an unmade script for The Million Dollar Hotel.

years.h: The Afghan Whigs play the bar band in Beautiful Girls
years.p: Greg Dulli's best friend Ted Demme directed the film; Dulli executive-produced the soundtrack. The band plays Barry White's Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe in a minor key.

eras.title: New Orleans, a fractured skull, a press release
eras.text: Greg Dulli moved south, started the Twilight Singers and made 1965, the Afghan Whigs' loosest, sexiest record. Then a fight outside an Austin club nearly killed him, and two years later the band ended by memo.

years.h: Greg Dulli moves to New Orleans, into Peter Buck's house
years.p: Dulli rents [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] guitarist [[Peter Buck|2bab20bf-8dab-4af8-b7b0-ba8e30860261]]'s place and starts [[The Twilight Singers|53a4de34-35ca-4ad0-aa4b-67382435ed69]] with local players. Michael Horrigan takes the Afghan Whigs' drum stool.

years.h: 1965: named for the year Greg Dulli and John Curley were born
years.p: Recorded at Daniel Lanois' New Orleans studio for Columbia, with film noir and Nas in the mix. The Afghan Whigs tour it opening for Aerosmith.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes Dulli was being treated for depression around the album's release.

years.h: Greg Dulli's skull fractured outside Liberty Lunch in Austin
years.p: After an Afghan Whigs show at Liberty Lunch, Dulli fought a stagehand and hit his head on the pavement. Wikipedia says he was left in a coma; he was back on tour in two months.
years.xp:
The Austin Chronicle reported the club's version: co-manager Mileah Jordan said Dulli was the aggressor, stayed after closing, and went at the stagehand with a two-by-four before the worker hit him once. Dulli was treated at Brackenridge Hospital. No charges were filed.

The band disputed the club's account, and MTV News later reported the Afghan Whigs suing the club.

years.h: The Afghan Whigs split by press release
years.p: The Afghan Whigs hadn't played since September 1999. The statement blames distance and family obligations; Greg Dulli calls it amicable, and soon co-buys the Short Stop bar in Los Angeles.

eras.title: See it now, or never
eras.text: Two new songs for a best-of, then five years of silence, then a festival booker made the call. The reunion was billed as a one-off and turned into a second career.

years.h: Back in a room for two songs: I'm a Soldier and Magazine
years.p: The Afghan Whigs regroup to cut new tracks for Unbreakable: A Retrospective 1990–2006, out on Rhino on June 5, 2007.

years.h: All Tomorrow's Parties announces the Afghan Whigs are back
years.p: The festival promoters break the news by press release: the first time the band has worked together since 2006.

q: We're doing this one time: See it now, or never see it again.
years.h: First full reunion show: the Bowery Ballroom, New York
years.p: The night after a Jimmy Fallon spot, the Afghan Whigs play Manhattan. Newsday called it possibly the band's greatest concert ever; the tour went on to sixteen countries.
years.xp: On Fallon they played See and Don't See, a 1970 soul song by Marie "Queenie" Lyons, and I'm Her Slave. Guitarist [[Dave Rosser|fd7c487f-f0fb-4fd1-b639-b5f3dcfa7742]] and multi-instrumentalist Rick Nelson came in for the reunion. SPIN's Steve Kandell wrote that Greg Dulli, at 47, was fitter and in better voice than in the band's heyday.

years.h: The Afghan Whigs give away a Frank Ocean cover, Lovecrimes
years.p: A free download of [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]]'s song, already a staple of the reunion shows.

years.h: Usher fronts the Afghan Whigs at SXSW
years.p: Usher heard the Frank Ocean cover and asked the Afghan Whigs to back him at the Fader Fort. Greg Dulli says he had to fix Usher's words in rehearsal.
years.xp: John Curley said that set made it likely the band would record again.

eras.title: Back on Sub Pop, minus old friends
eras.text: The second era now runs as long as the first. It brought three albums, a return to the label that signed them, and the loss of Rick McCollum from the band and Dave Rosser from the world.

years.h: Rick McCollum is no longer in the Afghan Whigs
years.p: The band announces McCollum's exit before its first album in 16 years. His pedal-soaked guitar had defined the sound.

years.h: Do to the Beast: the Afghan Whigs' first Top 40 album
years.p: Back on Sub Pop, it debuts at No. 32 on the Billboard 200. Guests include Usher's musical director Johnny Najera, Mark McGuire of Emeralds and Queens of the Stone Age's Alain Johannes.

years.h: Gentlemen at 21 scores 95 on Metacritic
years.p: The deluxe reissue of Gentlemen gets the best reviews of the Afghan Whigs' career. [[Patrick Keeler|0cb67e93-6b5f-4433-971c-6d4adb60d3d8]] of [[The Raconteurs|be407b02-f3e6-4ed5-9489-f8e5f0ab36dc]] is now on drums.

years.h: In Spades, cut at Rick Nelson's studio in New Orleans
years.p: Half the album was done in a week at Marigny Sound. Greg Dulli calls Prince, who died the year before, his North Star.

years.cap: The Afghan Whigs at Haldern Pop, August 2017, weeks after Rosser's death. Photo: Alexander Kellner
years.h: Guitarist Dave Rosser dies of colon cancer at 50
years.p: Rosser had played with the Afghan Whigs since the 2011 reunion and on both new albums. He died after a long illness, weeks after In Spades came out.

years.h: How Do You Burn? and a song in Gran Turismo 7
years.p: The first Afghan Whigs album in five years, on BMG. Lead single I'll Make You See God lands on the Gran Turismo 7 soundtrack; Blind Melon's Christopher Thorn joins on guitar.

years.h: Forty years on, a hometown show at Bogart's
years.p: The Afghan Whigs mark their 40th anniversary at Bogart's in Cincinnati, with drummer Bryan Lee Brown in for Patrick Keeler.

years.h: Soft Control, led by the single Jungle Roux
years.p: The fourth Afghan Whigs album since the reunion. Jungle Roux came out in June.
